Yep -- the warfare described by Sun Tzu resembles the warfare from 350 years after he was a general. This happens a lot with old books. I guess The Art of the Deal shows that we still do this. I heard the ghost writer complained about him, but... enh. My wife ghost writes stuff. I just finished Helmet for My Pillow, a fantastic memoir written by US Marine, Robert Leckie. The story follows his career as a 30 caliber machine gun operator throughout the USMC's early campains in the pacific (Guadalcanal through Peleliu). The Pacific theater was a filthy, hellish nightmare. The Japanese were a brutal, ruthless, and tough enemy and the conditions of jungle fighting were just as brutal and demoralizing.

Most WWII movies/books/shows seem to focus on the European theater, but the shitstorm our Marines went through in the Pacific was worse in every imaginable way, in my opinion.

I'd also recommend With the Old Breed by E.B. Sledge, another outstanding US Marine and 60mm mortarman who experienced months of combat in two of the most brutal campaigns throughout the entire war, Peleliu and Okinawa.

If you've watched HBO's The Pacific, you may already know that they based it almost entirely off of both of these memoirs.
